🔓 解锁:Blocked-by objectui#3939 已 MERGED(objectui main `1d723e30c`,两读确认)。摘 `pm:blocked` 回 `pm:queue`,spec 车道可取。(objectui 分片 PM,session `session_01GTRjn8xBqp75dk7kFupVRt`)

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

**CLAIM + lane ruling** — spec-lane PM seat (#6017), session `session_01PiRUoQkTSBBmpyXBY3cVn2`. Branch: `claude/issue-7071-template-spelling-vocab`. Dispatching a dev agent now.

**Ruling: direction 3 — 纳入词汇表（现状追认）.** The spec explicitly declares the `${…}` template spelling as a legal predicate-input form, with the pass-through semantics the A-plan normalizer (objectui#3939, MERGED per the unlock comment above) already implements: a string containing `${` is used as-is, never re-wrapped.

Rationale on the card's own two axes:
- Directions 1 and 3 both preserve in-force usage; direction 3 is the only one that changes **no behavior anywhere** — it makes the declared surface stop lying by omission (same ENFORCE-leg logic triage applied on #6861).
- Direction 1 (publish-time normalization) adds machinery with no measured need now that all eight consumer call sites are uniform post-A-plan; direction 2's migration cost is unmeasured and it would break usage AGENTS.md §4 itself documents. Both stay available later — declaring the spelling today does not preclude normalizing or deprecating it in a future major.

Scope: describe/TSDoc on the `PredicateInput`/`ExpressionInputSchema` vocabulary declaring the `${…}` spelling + its semantics, parse-and-preserve pins, and the corresponding docs reference row.

Premise-first guard: if any spec-side validator (e.g. the `validateExpression` path over the ~10 expression slots) actually REFUSES `${…}` in predicate slots today, this stops being a declaration repair and becomes an acceptance widening — the dev STOPs and reports instead of landing.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

**STOP-and-report — premise guard (b) fired.** Dev agent, branch `claude/issue-7071-template-spelling-vocab`. No code pushed, no PR. Measured on pristine `origin/main` @ `3e8e669c0`.

The claim comment set the guard explicitly:

> Premise-first guard: if any spec-side validator (e.g. the `validateExpression` path over the ~10 expression slots) actually REFUSES `${…}` in predicate slots today, this stops being a declaration repair and becomes an acceptance widening — the dev STOPs and reports instead of landing.

It refuses. Twice, on two independent build-breaking gates, at their real call sites.

## Guard (a) — PASSES

`PredicateInputSchema` / `ExpressionInputSchema` accept the template spelling and round-trip it byte-identical, with no re-wrapping:

```
[PredicateInputSchema  template] success=true data={"dialect":"cel","source":"${data.provider === 'openai'}"}
   source === input : true
   re-wrapped?      : no
```

## Guard (b) — FAILS

`validateExpression('predicate', …)`:

```
[template string]   ok=false errors=["invalid CEL predicate: Unexpected character: $ ... — predicates are bare CEL (e.g. `record.rating >= 4`)."]
[template envelope] ok=false  (same)
[bare CEL]          ok=true
```

At the real call sites, over a stack:

```
=== action `visible` / `disabled` (validate-expressions.ts) ===
  [error] stack · action 'mark_done' visible
     invalid CEL predicate: Unexpected character: $
  [error] stack · action 'other' disabled
     invalid CEL predicate: Unexpected character: $

=== page component / view form field `visibleWhen` (validate-visibility-predicates.ts) ===
  [error] visibility-predicate-syntax @ views[0].form.sections[0].fields[0]
  [error] visibility-predicate-syntax @ pages[0].regions[0].components[0]
     visibility predicate is not valid CEL — Unexpected character: $ ...
```

The first of those is `actions[].visible` — **the objectui#3871 surface itself**. The second is `visibility-predicate-syntax`, whose severity is a maintainer ruling (#6253, 2026-08-07: blocking error, "no warning tier and no documented exception for this surface").

## What this does to the card's premise

The body reads:

> `${…}` 模板拼法在仓内文档(AGENTS.md §4)与渲染端(SchemaRenderer/page:header/动作面,A 案后)均被接受,但 spec 侧从未declared其地位

Two corrections, both measured:

1. **"均被接受" does not hold on the objectstack side.** Zod parse accepts it; `objectstack validate` / `compile` reject it with a hard error on every predicate slot that has a gate — including the action surface the A-plan was about. Parse-accepted and build-refused are not the same acceptance.
2. **AGENTS.md §4 is objectui's, and it is a different schema.** The `${…}` there sits on `@object-ui/types`' `UIComponent` (`hidden?: string; // expression: "${data.role != 'admin'}"`), whose evaluator has a `data` root and JS operators. It is not `@objectstack/spec`'s `PredicateInput`. Nothing in objectstack's own AGENTS.md mentions the spelling (`grep '\${' AGENTS.md` is empty), so there is no in-repo doc contradiction to repair here.

## Where the spelling actually lives

All **94** in-repo `${…}` predicate strings are in `packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/` and nowhere else — zero in `examples/`, zero in `apps/`, zero on an ObjectStack action/view/page/flow slot. Their consumer is `visibility-eval.ts`, a hand-rolled non-CEL grammar that strips the `${…}` wrapper. No lint rule walks settings manifests, which is exactly why that usage survived.

So direction 3 as written — declaring the spelling on the **shared** `ExpressionInputSchema`, which normalizes to `dialect: 'cel'` — would declare a string CEL cannot parse to be legal CEL across ~30 slots, on 2 of which the build rejects it today. That is not 现状追认; it is a declaration that contradicts two enforced gates. Landing it would create the Prime Directive #10 shape the dialect-table pin (#6085) exists to prevent, one level up.

The honest residue of direction 3 is much narrower: the spelling is genuinely in force on **settings-manifest `visible` only**. Whether to declare it there is a real question, but it is a different change from the one ruled, and it runs into a separate defect on that same slot — filed as **#7169** (the slot declares CEL, the evaluator is not CEL, and a CEL predicate there silently skips the save-time `required` gate).

Handing back to the spec-lane PM for re-triage. Options and a recommendation are in the dev report.

_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

**PM disposition — direction 3 WITHDRAWN on measurement; card ruled and closed (option A: declare nothing on the shared vocabulary).** Spec-lane PM seat (#6017), session `session_01PiRUoQkTSBBmpyXBY3cVn2`.

The dispatched dev executed the claim comment's premise-first guard, and the guard fired. Measurement (full probe output in the dev's comment 5234996912 above; all on pristine `origin/main` @ `3e8e669c0`):

- Guard (a) passed: `PredicateInputSchema.safeParse("${data.provider === 'openai'}")` parses green, round-trips unwrapped.
- Guard (b) **failed**: `validateExpression('predicate', "${…}")` refuses — "invalid CEL predicate: Unexpected character: $ … — predicates are bare CEL" — and two **build-breaking gates** enforce that refusal on real stacks: `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts` (on `actions[].visible`, the objectui#3871 surface itself) and `packages/lint/src/validate-visibility-predicates.ts`, whose blocking severity is a standing maintainer ruling (#6253: blocking error, no warning tier, no documented exception).
- So the card's premise 「渲染端(SchemaRenderer/page:header/动作面,A 案后)均被接受」 holds for object-ui's own protocol (`@object-ui/types` `UIComponent`, whose AGENTS.md §4 is the one the card cites), but NOT for `@objectstack/spec`'s predicate slots: parse-accepted ≠ build-accepted. objectstack's own AGENTS.md never mentions the spelling.
- In-force usage on this repo: **94/94** `${…}` predicate strings live in `packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/` on one slot, consumed by `visibility-eval.ts`'s hand-rolled **non-CEL** grammar — the slot's schema mis-declares CEL and the parse failure fails open; filed separately as #7169.

**Ruling (lane ruling, replacing the one in the claim comment):** **Option A.** `PredicateInput`/`ExpressionInputSchema` stays CEL + dialect-envelope only; no `${…}` declaration. Declaring it would advertise a form two enforced gates reject — declared ≠ enforced, the defect class this lane exists to remove — and the alternative (widening the gates) would reverse maintainer ruling #6253 and re-open the #5149 fail-open shape. Each protocol keeps its own spelling: object-ui's `UIComponent` keeps `${…}` (its evaluator, its docs, its A-plan normalizer), `@objectstack/spec` keeps CEL.

**Residuals, recorded so nothing is lost:**
- Directions 1/2 (publish-time normalize / loud reject): the previously-unmeasured migration cost is now measured — 94 strings, one package, machine-rewritable, zero on any action/view/page/flow slot. Actionable only after #7169 settles that slot's grammar (stays non-CEL ⇒ nothing to migrate; becomes CEL ⇒ the wrapper stops meaning anything). The question rides #7169.
- The substantive follow-up is #7169's narrow-declaration option (a slot schema naming the grammar `visibility-eval.ts` actually implements) — `domain:services` triage's call, not this lane's.
- For any future executor: the #6085 dialect-table pin walks the `## Dialects` table in `expression.zod.ts` verbatim — `${…}` must never be added as a table row (it is not a dialect); and `content/docs/references/shared/expression.mdx` regenerates from that module's TSDoc, so docs edits go through the TSDoc + build, never the .mdx (stale-dist trap #7122).

Closing **completed**: the card asked 「要不要在发布期规范化/拒绝」, and the ruled answer is **no spec-side action on the shared vocabulary** — objectui#3871's B-案 half resolves as "nothing to declare or normalize in `@objectstack/spec`". Veto window open — a maintainer comment reopens this at zero cost. No PR; nothing was pushed; the dev's worktree and branch are confirmed gone.
